claim: This test is a test used in diagnosing the disease "Usher syndrome, type 4".
context: diagnosis: Pure-Tone Audiometry — Audiometric assessment documents the late-onset, progressive sensorineural hearing loss that is the auditory component of USH4, distinguishing it from the congenital loss of types 1 and 2 and the first-decade-onset loss of type 3.

loinc_label: Hearing threshold Ear - right --4000 Hz
claim: This test is a test used in diagnosing the disease "deafness, aminoglycoside-induced".
context: diagnosis: Clinical audiologic and exposure assessment — Document hearing thresholds, onset, aminoglycoside history and the maternal family history. Age-appropriate audiometry and objective tests when needed characterize sensorineural loss; high-frequency testing can identify injury that conventional speech-frequency tests miss. A failed neonatal screening test alone is not proof of permanent aminoglycoside deafness.

loinc_label: Corynebacterium toxin [Presence] in Specimen by Immune diffusion (ID)
claim: This test is a test used in diagnosing the disease "diphtheria".
context: diagnosis: Culture and toxigenicity testing — Diagnosis is clinical and is confirmed by isolating a member of the C. diphtheriae species complex and then demonstrating toxin production. Species identification alone is insufficient, because tox-bearing isolates may still fail to express toxin: in the French Guiana series five isolates were tox-positive by PCR yet all were negative by Elek test. Phenotypic toxigenicity testing therefore governs whether antitoxin is indicated.

loinc_label: Treponema pallidum Ab [Presence] in Serum by Immunoassay
claim: A result of [POSITIVE] on this test indicates the disease "syphilis".
context: Reactive — Treponemal antibody usually remains reactive for life after infection, treated or not, so a reactive result does not distinguish active syphilis from a serological scar. It also does not stage the infection: the same result is returned in primary, secondary, latent and tertiary disease.

loinc_label: Thyrotropin [Units/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Detection limit <= 0.05 mIU/L
claim: A result of [ABOVE_TARGET, HIGH] on this test indicates the phenotype "Elevated circulating thyroid-stimulating hormone concentration".
context: Above the adult reference interval [4.0, )  — After total thyroid ablation. Applying this goal to an untreated person is a clinical error. Neither source names an analyser, beyond requiring a functional sensitivity that can resolve the goal. — Under-replaced, and now also biochemically hypothyroid. This is where an elevated TSH can honestly be asserted. ‖ Elevated [4.0, )  — Consensus adult reference interval, retained after reviewing proposals to lower the upper limit. — One band, three targets, two relations. With a normal free T4 this is compensated (subclinical) hypothyroidism, and the same number argues against hyperthyroidism, in which TSH is suppressed rather than raised. It argues against rather than rules out, because a TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma and resistance to thyroid hormone both raise TSH and thyroid hormones together.

loinc_label: Digoxin>12 hours post dose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
claim: A result of [SUBTHERAPEUTIC, THERAPEUTIC] on this test argues against the disease "digitalis poisoning".
context: At the titration target [0.5, 0.9) nanogram per milliliter — Already on maintenance digoxin. It does not apply to anyone not taking digoxin, in whom an undetectable level is the expected result rather than a subtherapeutic one. — At the concentration treatment aims for. `outcome: THERAPEUTIC` is a claim about the drug being at goal, which is why it is not `NORMAL`: there is no reference interval for digoxin to be within. ‖ Below the titration target [, 0.5) nanogram per milliliter — Already on maintenance digoxin. It does not apply to anyone not taking digoxin, in whom an undetectable level is the expected result rather than a subtherapeutic one. — Below the concentration the trial titrates to. In a treated patient this reads as under-dosing; in an untreated patient it is simply the absence of the drug, which this record cannot distinguish and `population` has to.
